objective_pt: Tell an anecdote vividly: mix narrative tenses (past perfect, past continuous), use precise verbs ("stumbled", "glanced") and build suspense ("It was only when... that...").

teacher.goal_pt: Elicit a short anecdote and listen for tense control and detail.
prompts: Tell me about a time something went completely wrong on a trip.
What had you expected to happen?
watchFor: Everything in the simple past, with no background (past continuous) or earlier events (past perfect).
"Then... then... then..." as the only linker.

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat, slowing down slightly before the twist.
exercises.prompt: I'd been waiting for an hour when I realised I was at the wrong station.
accepted: I'd been waiting for an hour when I realised I was at the wrong station
I'd been waiting for an hour when I realized I was at the wrong station
I had been waiting for an hour when I realised I was at the wrong station

exercises.instruction_pt: Which sentence makes it clear that the film started before they arrived?
options: When we arrived, the film started.
When we arrived, the film had already started.
When we arrived, the film was starting.
exercises.explanation_pt: The past perfect ("had started") shows the earlier action. With the simple past, the film starts when they arrive.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Quando cheguei, todo mundo já tinha ido embora."
accepted: When I arrived, everyone had already left
When I got there, everyone had already left
When I arrived, everybody had already left
When I got there, everybody had already gone
When I arrived, everyone had already gone
By the time I arrived, everyone had already left
By the time I got there, everyone had left
By the time I got there, everyone had already gone home

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Everyone" is grammatically singular, but here the tense is the issue: use the past perfect, "everyone had already left".
commonErrors.correction_en: When I arrived, everyone had already left.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Já tinha ido" is an action before another past action, so the past perfect is clearer: "had already left".
commonErrors.correction_en: When I arrived, everyone had already left.

teacher.goal_pt: Replace generic verbs (go, look, say) with precise narrative verbs: stumble, glance, mutter, rush, stare.
prompts: Show me the difference between "glance" and "stare".
When did you last rush somewhere?
watchFor: "Realise" used for "perceber" correctly, but "notice" vs "realise" confused.

exercises.example_en: She glanced at her watch and frowned.
We stumbled across a tiny restaurant in the old town.
He muttered something about the weather and left.

exercises.instruction_pt: Match each storytelling verb with its meaning.
Say this in natural English: "Foi aí que eu percebi que tinha esquecido o passaporte."
accepted: That's when I realised I'd forgotten my passport
That's when I realized I had forgotten my passport
That's when I realised I'd left my passport behind
It was then that I realised I'd forgotten my passport
That was when I realised I'd forgotten my passport
That's when it hit me that I'd forgotten my passport
That's when I noticed I'd forgotten my passport

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Perceber" (to become aware) is "realise", not "perceive", which is formal and about the senses.
commonErrors.correction_en: That's when I realised I'd forgotten my passport.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: English uses possessives with personal belongings: "my passport", not "the passport".
commonErrors.correction_en: That's when I realised I'd forgotten my passport.

teacher.goal_pt: Pacing and pausing for suspense; the three "-ed" endings in narrative verbs.
prompts: Say "And then... nothing." with a dramatic pause.
watchFor: Adding an extra syllable to "rushed" ("rush-ed") or "glanced" ("glan-ced").

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat. "Rushed" and "stopped" end in /t/, one syllable each.
exercises.prompt: I rushed to the door and stopped dead.
accepted: I rushed to the door and stopped dead

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat with a short pause after "door" to build suspense.
exercises.prompt: And there, standing at the door, was my old boss.
accepted: And there, standing at the door, was my old boss

exercises.instruction_pt: Which verb has an extra syllable in the past tense?
exercises.explanation_pt: Verbs ending in /t/ or /d/ add /ɪd/: wai-ted. "Glanced" (/t/) and "stumbled" (/d/) don't add a syllable.

teacher.goal_pt: Follow the order of events in a story told out of sequence and react naturally.
prompts: How would you react if a friend told you this?
watchFor: Assuming events happened in the order they were mentioned.
Reacting with just "OK" instead of showing interest.

exercises.listen: By the time the taxi turned up, I'd already missed the flight, and I'd been arguing with the airline for twenty minutes.
options: The speaker started arguing with the airline.
exercises.explanation_pt: Both past perfects are earlier than the taxi, and the argument came after missing the flight.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen to your friend and react with interest, asking what happened next.
exercises.listen: So I opened the door, and guess who was standing there?
accepted: Who?
No idea, who?
Who was it?
I have no idea. Who was it?
Go on, who was it?
Who was standing there?
Don't tell me it was your ex!
Who? Tell me!
I can't guess. Who?
Who was there?

commonErrors.explanation_pt: In a direct question, the verb comes before "there": "Who was there?".
commonErrors.correction_en: Who was there?

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen and say what you think had happened to the speaker's phone.
exercises.listen: I got home and the phone wasn't in my bag. It turned out I'd left it on the bus.
accepted: You'd left it on the bus
You had left it on the bus
You left it on the bus
It was on the bus
You left your phone on the bus
You'd left your phone on the bus
It had been left on the bus
It was still on the bus

commonErrors.explanation_pt: We say "on the bus" (also "on the train", "on the plane"), not "in the bus". And "esquecer em um lugar" is usually "leave".
commonErrors.correction_en: You'd left it on the bus.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: With buses, trains and planes, English uses "on": "on the bus".
commonErrors.correction_en: You'd left it on the bus.

teacher.goal_pt: Tell a 1–2 minute anecdote with setting, complication, climax and resolution.
prompts: Tell me about the most embarrassing moment of your life.
Where were you and what were you doing at the time?
How did it end? Would you do anything differently?

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Eu estava andando para casa quando começou a chover."
accepted: I was walking home when it started to rain
I was walking home when it started raining
I was walking home when it began to rain
I was walking home when it began raining
I was on my way home when it started to rain
I was walking back home when it started raining

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Home" works like an adverb after verbs of movement: "walk home", "go home", without "to".
commonErrors.correction_en: I was walking home when it started to rain.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: English needs a subject for weather: "it started to rain".
commonErrors.correction_en: I was walking home when it started to rain.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Só quando cheguei ao hotel é que percebi o erro."
accepted: It was only when I got to the hotel that I realised my mistake
It was only when I arrived at the hotel that I realised my mistake
It was only when I got to the hotel that I noticed the mistake
It wasn't until I got to the hotel that I realised my mistake
It wasn't until I arrived at the hotel that I realised the mistake
Only when I got to the hotel did I realise my mistake
Only when I arrived at the hotel did I realise my mistake
I only realised my mistake when I got to the hotel

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Chegar a" is "arrive at" (a building) or "arrive in" (a city), never "arrive to". Or say "get to".
commonErrors.correction_en: It was only when I got to the hotel that I realised my mistake.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: If you start with "Only when...", invert the main clause: "...did I realise". Or use "It was only when... that I realised".
commonErrors.correction_en: Only when I got to the hotel did I realise my mistake.

exercises.instruction_pt: Put the words in order to start a story.
accepted: You'll never guess what happened to me yesterday

exercises.instruction_pt: Tell the story in one or two minutes, with as much vivid detail as you can.
exercises.prompt_en: Tell me about a time when a small mistake led to something unexpected, good or bad. Set the scene first.
guidelines_pt: Set the scene with the past continuous: "I was sitting...".
Use the past perfect for what had happened before.
Use at least two precise verbs (glance, rush, stumble, mutter...).
Build up to the climax: "It was only when... that...", then say how it ended.

teacher.goal_pt: Check narrative tenses and prepositions of transport and arrival.
prompts: What were you doing at 8 pm yesterday?
What had you done before breakfast today?

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Ele parecia que não dormia havia dias."
accepted: He looked like he hadn't slept for days
He looked as if he hadn't slept for days
He looked as though he hadn't slept for days
He looked like he hadn't slept in days
He seemed like he hadn't slept for days
It looked like he hadn't slept for days
It looked as if he hadn't slept in days

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Ele parecia que..." is "He looked like..." / "He looked as if...", not "He seemed that".
commonErrors.correction_en: He looked as if he hadn't slept for days.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: For a period up to a past moment, use the past perfect: "hadn't slept for days".
commonErrors.correction_en: He looked as if he hadn't slept for days.

exercises.sentence: We finally arrived ___ the airport at midnight.
accepted: at

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Use "arrive at" for a specific place (airport, station, hotel); "arrive in" for cities and countries.
commonErrors.correction_en: We finally arrived at the airport at midnight.

exercises.explanation_pt: "Glance" is a quick look. "Stare" and "gaze" are long looks.

exercises.prompt: Looking back, it was one of the best things that ever happened to me.
accepted: Looking back, it was one of the best things that ever happened to me

practice.meaning_pt: cair a ficha, alguém perceber de repente
practice.example_en: It slowly dawned on me that nobody was coming.

practice.meaning_pt: perder o fôlego (de susto ou surpresa)
practice.example_en: Everyone gasped when the curtain fell.
He staggered out of the taxi, half asleep.
Out of the blue, my cousin called from Japan.

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat. Stress "dawned" and "oven".
practice.prompt: It suddenly dawned on me that I'd left the oven on.
accepted: It suddenly dawned on me that I'd left the oven on
It suddenly dawned on me that I had left the oven on

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat. Slow down on "when the lights went out" to build suspense.
practice.prompt: We'd barely sat down when the lights went out.
accepted: We'd barely sat down when the lights went out
We had barely sat down when the lights went out

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with natural rhythm and stress.
practice.prompt: Out of the blue, a stranger tapped me on the shoulder.
accepted: Out of the blue, a stranger tapped me on the shoulder
Out of the blue, a stranger tapped me on my shoulder

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with natural rhythm and stress.
practice.prompt: I was halfway through my speech when my mind went blank.
accepted: I was halfway through my speech when my mind went blank
I was halfway through my speech when my mind went completely blank

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with natural rhythm and stress.
practice.prompt: To cut a long story short, we missed the flight.
accepted: To cut a long story short, we missed the flight
To cut a long story short, we missed our flight
Long story short, we missed the flight

practice.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Eu já tinha saído quando ele ligou."
accepted: I'd already left when he called
I had already left when he called
I'd already gone when he called
I'd already left by the time he called
I had already left by the time he called
I'd already left when he rang
When he called, I'd already left
When he called, I had already left

commonErrors.explanation_pt: For the earlier of two past actions, use the past perfect: "I'd already left when he called".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'd already left when he called.

practice.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "De repente, todo mundo ficou em silêncio."
accepted: Suddenly, everyone went quiet
Suddenly, everybody went quiet
Suddenly, everyone went silent
All of a sudden, everyone went quiet
All of a sudden, everybody went silent
Suddenly, everyone fell silent
All of a sudden, everyone fell silent
Suddenly the whole room went quiet

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Todo mundo" is "everyone" or "everybody".
commonErrors.correction_en: Suddenly, everyone went quiet.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Ficar em silêncio" (suddenly) is "go quiet" or "fall silent".
commonErrors.correction_en: Everyone fell silent.

practice.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Eu mal podia acreditar no que estava vendo."
accepted: I could hardly believe what I was seeing
I could barely believe what I was seeing
I could hardly believe my eyes
I could barely believe my eyes
I could scarcely believe what I was seeing
I couldn't believe what I was seeing
I could hardly believe what I was looking at
I could hardly believe what I saw

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Acreditar no que" is "believe what". "Believe in" means having faith in something.
commonErrors.correction_en: I could hardly believe what I was seeing.

practice.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Enquanto a gente jantava, alguém bateu na porta."
accepted: While we were having dinner, someone knocked on the door
While we were having dinner, somebody knocked on the door
While we were eating dinner, someone knocked on the door
While we were having dinner, someone knocked at the door
We were having dinner when someone knocked on the door
We were having dinner when somebody knocked at the door
While we were having dinner, there was a knock at the door
While we were having supper, someone knocked on the door

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Bater na porta" is "knock on/at the door". "Beat" means to hit hard repeatedly.
commonErrors.correction_en: Someone knocked on the door.

practice.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Ele ficou parado na porta, olhando para mim."
accepted: He stood in the doorway, staring at me
He stood in the doorway, looking at me
He was standing in the doorway, staring at me
He was standing in the doorway, looking at me
He stood at the door, staring at me
He was standing at the door, staring at me
He stood in the doorway and stared at me
He stood frozen in the doorway, staring at me

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Ficar parado" is "stand (still)", not "stay stopped".
commonErrors.correction_en: He stood in the doorway, staring at me.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen and continue the story: say you realised your passport had expired.
practice.listen: So what happened when you got to the airport?
accepted: I realised my passport had expired
I realized my passport had expired
I found out my passport had expired
That's when I realised my passport had expired
That's when I realized my passport had expired
It turned out my passport had expired
I discovered that my passport had expired
I realised that my passport had expired
I realized that my passport had expired
Well, it turned out my passport had expired

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Say the passport "had expired" or "was out of date".
commonErrors.correction_en: I realised my passport had expired.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen and describe your reaction vividly in one sentence.
practice.listen: How did you feel when you saw him standing there?
accepted: I froze
I just froze
I was speechless
I was completely speechless
I couldn't believe my eyes
My heart was pounding
My heart skipped a beat
I was lost for words
I nearly burst into tears
I was absolutely stunned
I stood there, completely stunned
I was *
I felt *
I just *
My heart *

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Fiquei sem palavras" is "I was speechless" or "I was lost for words".
commonErrors.correction_en: I was speechless.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen and continue the story: say you grabbed your bag and rushed out of the house.
practice.listen: And then what did you do?
accepted: I grabbed my bag and rushed out of the house
I grabbed my bag and ran out of the house
I grabbed my bag and dashed out of the house
I grabbed my bag and rushed out
I picked up my bag and rushed out of the house
I just grabbed my bag and rushed out of the house
Then I grabbed my bag and rushed out of the house

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Pegar" an object is "pick up" (or "grab"): "I picked up my bag".
commonErrors.correction_en: I grabbed my bag and rushed out of the house.

practice.instruction_pt: Tell a short anecdote in about a minute.
practice.prompt_en: Tell me about a time when something didn't go according to plan.
guidelines_pt: Set the scene with the past continuous: "I was ... when ...".
Use the past perfect for background: "I'd forgotten..."
Use at least two precise verbs (glance, rush, freeze, mutter).

practice.instruction_pt: Role-play: tell your friend what happened, adding detail and suspense.
practice.scene_pt: You meet a friend for dinner after a very strange day.

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say you've had the strangest day.
accepted: I've had the strangest day
I've had the weirdest day
I've had the strangest day ever
I've had such a strange day
I've just had the strangest day
You won't believe the day I've had
I have had the strangest day

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Strange" forms "stranger / the strangest".
commonErrors.correction_en: I've had the strangest day.

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say you were driving to a meeting when your car broke down in the middle of nowhere.
accepted: I was driving to a meeting when my car broke down in the middle of nowhere
I was on my way to a meeting when my car broke down in the middle of nowhere
I was driving to a meeting and my car broke down in the middle of nowhere
My car broke down in the middle of nowhere while I was driving to a meeting
I was driving to a meeting when the car broke down in the middle of nowhere

commonErrors.explanation_pt: A car "breaks down" (quebra). "Break" alone means to smash into pieces.
commonErrors.correction_en: My car broke down in the middle of nowhere.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Oh no! What did you do?

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say your phone had died, so you had to walk to the nearest village.
accepted: My phone had died, so I had to walk to the nearest village
My phone was dead, so I had to walk to the nearest village
My phone had run out of battery, so I had to walk to the nearest village
My phone had died, so I had to walk to the closest village
My phone had died, so I ended up walking to the nearest village
My battery had died, so I had to walk to the nearest village

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Sem bateria" is "dead" or "out of battery".
commonErrors.correction_en: My phone had died.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: You're kidding! And did you make it to the meeting?

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say that, believe it or not, the meeting had been cancelled anyway.
accepted: Believe it or not, the meeting had been cancelled anyway
Believe it or not, the meeting had been canceled anyway
Believe it or not, it had been cancelled anyway
Believe it or not, they'd cancelled the meeting anyway
Believe it or not, the meeting had been called off anyway
Believe it or not, the meeting had already been cancelled

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The fixed phrase is "believe it or not".
commonErrors.correction_en: Believe it or not, the meeting had been cancelled anyway.

practice.instruction_pt: Choose the best verb form: "By the time we arrived, the film ___."
practice.explanation_pt: The film started before we arrived, so we use the past perfect: "had started".

practice.instruction_pt: Which verb describes walking unsteadily, almost falling?
practice.explanation_pt: "Stagger" is walking unsteadily; "stroll" is a relaxed walk; "march" is walking with firm steps.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen. What was already happening when the phone rang?
practice.listen: I was just about to leave when the phone rang, and everything changed.
options: She was talking on the phone.
practice.explanation_pt: "I was just about to leave when..." describes the situation that was in place when the phone rang.

practice.instruction_pt: Complete with one word.
practice.sentence: I ___ walking home when I heard a scream.
accepted: was

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Past continuous with "I": "I was walking".
commonErrors.correction_en: I was walking home when I heard a scream.

practice.instruction_pt: Complete with one word.
practice.sentence: Little did I know ___ my life was about to change.
accepted: that

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The clause after "know" is introduced by "that".
commonErrors.correction_en: Little did I know that my life was about to change.

practice.instruction_pt: Put the words in order to make a dramatic sentence.
accepted: No sooner had I sat down than the phone rang

practice.instruction_pt: Match each storytelling expression with its meaning.
